artifact_links.text: `GET/PUT /limits/{kind}/...` accept `kind: str`; an absent row returns `404 unknown_kind` instead of FastAPI's 422 path validation (SCN-LIM-01.2, SCN-LIM-06.3). The PUT body is read as a raw dict and validated as exactly three strict positive integers with `review_threshold <= per_transfer <= daily`; any missing key, extra key, bool, non-integer, zero or negative value raises `422 invalid_limits` through the existing `DomainError` handler. This is chosen over a Pydantic model because a model failure would emit FastAPI's default 422 body rather than the required `{"error":{"code":"invalid_limits"}}` (SCN-LIM-01.2). PUT replaces all three columns and writes the audit row in the same write transaction (SCN-LIM-01.1, SCN-LIM-06.1, SCN-LIM-06.3).
artifact_links.reason: The decision specifies sender-kind rules, required limits input, replacement, and preserved domain error shape.

artifact_links.text: `Ledger.transfer` keeps one write session and performs checks in this order: (1) idempotency lookup/conflict, (2) source and destination existence, (3) self-transfer, (4) source-closed and destination-closed, (5) sender-kind `per_transfer`, (6) UTC-day `daily` sum, (7) sender debit, (8) recipient credit only when not in review, (9) insert transfer with `completed` or `pending_review`, (10) store the idempotency response. The idempotency lookup precedes validation so a replayed key returns the cached 201 even if the account state later differs (SCN-LIM-03.1). Each rejection occurs before any debit/insert, so balances, history and daily usage stay intact (SCN-LIM-01.3, SCN-LIM-01.4, SCN-LIM-02.1, SCN-LIM-02.2). When several violations coexist, this documented order decides which single error code is returned.
artifact_links.reason: The transfer decision explicitly describes self-transfers, closed destinations, and stopping before any ledger write.

artifact_links.text: `idempotency_keys` is keyed by `(sender, key)` and stores destination, amount and the exact 201 JSON. Lookup within the write transaction compares destination and amount: equal returns the cached response, different raises `409 idempotency_conflict` (SCN-LIM-03.1, SCN-LIM-03.2). The cache is written only after the transfer succeeds, so a failed request reserves nothing (SCN-LIM-03.3). Because writes already use `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, simultaneous repeats serialize: the first commits the row, the second reads it; restart persistence comes from SQLite (SCN-LIM-03.3). A missing or empty header means no lookup and every success creates a new row (SCN-LIM-03.2).
artifact_links.reason: The decision describes sender-scoped responses, exact replays, payload conflicts, transaction serialization, and restart persistence.

artifact_links.text: A transfer is `pending_review` only when `amount > review_threshold`; equality completes immediately (SCN-LIM-04.1). For pending rows the sender is debited and the recipient untouched at creation. `POST /transfers/{id}/confirm` opens a write transaction, loads the row, raises `404 transfer_not_found` or `409 already_completed` as appropriate, credits the recipient, updates the status to `completed`, and returns the reloaded record, leaving identity fields and `created_at` unchanged (SCN-LIM-04.2, SCN-LIM-04.3). Serialization by `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` makes the credit happen exactly once under concurrent confirmations.
artifact_links.reason: The decision specifies the review threshold, immediate debit, the confirmation transaction, and confirmation errors.

artifact_links.text: `GET /accounts/{id}/history` parses `offset`, `limit`, `from`, `to`, `type` and `status` manually from the request query string so every validation failure returns `422 invalid_history_query` (SCN-LIM-05.3). Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`; `from` lower bound is `T00:00:00Z` and `to` upper bound is exclusive at the next midnight, making both bounds inclusive (SCN-LIM-05.2). Direction maps to `destination = account` or `source = account`; status maps to the stored value; all predicates combine with AND. The repository runs a COUNT with the same predicates for `total`, then a descending-ID SELECT with `LIMIT/OFFSET`, returning `{items, total, offset, limit}` with defaults 0 and 50 (SCN-LIM-05.1, SCN-LIM-05.2). Existing callers that read `items` keep working.
artifact_links.reason: The decision describes filtered paginated operation history, preservation of the items portion, and ordering.

artifact_links.text: Every successful PUT that changes at least one value inserts `before_json` and `after_json` serialized from complete rule dicts (including `kind`) plus `at = format_timestamp(clock())`, in the same transaction as the rule update (SCN-LIM-06.1, SCN-LIM-06.3). A validation failure changes nothing; a PUT repeating the current configuration updates nothing and appends no row (SCN-LIM-06.2). `GET /limits/{kind}/audit` selects rows by kind ordered by increasing `id` and returns `{"items":[{"before":...,"after":...,"at":...}]}`; unknown kinds use the same repository lookup and return `404 unknown_kind`.
artifact_links.reason: The decision specifies the per-kind, ordered, transactional audit snapshots and domain errors.
